highlights:
Here is how Meta Platforms performed in the just reported quarter in terms of the metrics most widely monitored and projected by Wall Street analysts: 

- Family daily active people (DAP): $3.64 billion versus $3.64 billion estimated by four analysts on average. 
- Headcount: 66,775 compared to the 69,468 average estimate based on four analysts. 
- Average Revenue Per Person (ARPP): $17.72 compared to the $17.46 average estimate based on two analysts. 
- Advertising Revenue- US & Canada: $28.44 billion versus the four-analyst average estimate of $27.64 billion. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of +33.3%. 
- Geographical Revenue by User- US & Canada: $28.91 billion compared to the $28.07 billion average estimate based on four analysts. The reported number represents a change of +32.9% year over year. 
- Geographical Revenue by User- Asia-Pacific: $11.89 billion versus $12.6 billion estimated by three analysts on average. Compared to the year-ago quarter, this number represents a +15.8% change. 
- Advertising Revenue- Rest of the World: $8.86 billion versus $8.3 billion estimated by three analysts on average. Compared to the year-ago quarter, this number represents a +33% change. 
- Geographical Revenue by User- Rest of World: $9.34 billion compared to the $8.83 billion average estimate based on three analysts. The reported number represents a change of +34.4% year over year. 
- Revenue- Advertising: $63.06 billion versus the eight-analyst average estimate of $61.9 billion. The reported number represents a year-over-year change of +25.9%. 
- Revenue- Other revenue: $1.1 billion versus $1.16 billion estimated by seven analysts on average. Compared to the year-ago quarter, this number represents a +59% change. 
- Revenue- Family of Apps (FoA): $64.16 billion versus $63.02 billion estimated by seven analysts on average. Compared to the year-ago quarter, this number represents a +26.4% change. 
- Revenue- Reality Labs: $443 million compared to the $464.57 million average estimate based on six analysts. The reported number represents a change of -5.7% year over year.

results.title: Meta Employee Headcount Falls to 66,775 in Q3 2026
results.author: Apoorv Tamrakar
highlights:
Meta employee headcount was 66,775 on September 30, 2026, down 15% year-over-year, per its Q3 2026 earnings release filed with the SEC.

By Apoorv Tamrakar · LinkedIn · Oct 26, 2026 · 4 min read

Meta reported 66,775 employees as of September 30, 2026. That is down 15% from a year earlier and 11.5% below the 75,472 it had at June 30. The count appears in the company's third-quarter results, published October 21, 2026 and filed with the SEC as Exhibit 99.1. The same results put 2026 capital spending at $135 billion to $145 billion, while Reality Labs losses are expected to shrink to $18 billion to $19 billion this year.

## How many people does Meta employ now?

Meta's release gives the count in one line: "Headcount was 66,775 as of September 30, 2026, a decrease of 15% year-over-year." The table sets that figure against the June 30 count from Meta's second-quarter release, and shows the calculated change.

| Measure | Value | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Headcount, June 30, 2026 | 75,472 | Meta Q2 2026 results |
| Headcount, September 30, 2026 | 66,775 | Meta Q3 2026 results |
| Change in the quarter | -8,697 (-11.5%) | Calculated from the two counts above |
| Change year-over-year | -15% (reported, rounded) | Meta Q3 2026 results |
| Implied September 30, 2025 headcount | About 78,100 to 79,000 | Calculated from the rounded 15% decline |

The year-earlier range is wide because Meta rounds the percentage. A 14.5% to 15.5% decline on 66,775 employees implies a base between about 78,100 and 79,000.

## Why did headcount fall in the third quarter?

Meta's second-quarter results said its reported headcount "includes approximately 8,000 employees impacted by the May 2026 headcount reduction, the majority of whom will no longer be reflected in our headcount by the end of the third quarter of 2026."

The quarterly net drop of 8,697 is larger than 8,000, but the two numbers measure different things. Net headcount reflects hires, departures and reductions together. Meta's headline count does not explain the movement by cause, so the reduction cannot be read as the full story of the change.

...

## What's still unclear?

- Whether contract and part-time staff are counted. The headline figure does not say whether contractors or part-time workers are in the 66,775. That affects how the decline should be read.
- Whether the May reduction is fully out of the count. Meta's second-quarter release says most of the roughly 8,000 affected employees will no longer be reflected by the end of Q3. The third-quarter release does not say how many remain in the 66,775.
- Conflicting third-party headcount estimates. Third-party data providers publish headcount estimates that differ from Meta's filing. This post uses only Meta's own filing for the current count.
- The weakest point of this argument. Quarter-end headcount and capex show direction, not intent. Meta's filings do not state how many people it plans to hire for AI, so the link between spending and jobs remains an inference.

results.title: Meta Headcount Fell 15% to 66,775 in a Year After May Cuts as AI Spending Climbs
results.author: Jobs, Hire Staff Reporter
highlights:
Meta ended September with 66,775 employees, down 15% from a year earlier, according to its third-quarter earnings release. The release does not explain the decline or mention restructuring. On the earnings call, Chief Financial Officer Susan Li gave a narrower answer: "We ended Q3 with over 66 thousand employees, down 12% from Q2 following the May 2026 headcount reduction," according to a call transcript.

So the cause of the drop is not a mystery, even if the filing is silent. Meta cut jobs in May. What remains unclear is how large the cuts were in total, what the company plans next, and what the decline says about the kind of company Meta wants to be.

...

Working backward from Meta's own figures gives rough numbers. A 15% year-over-year drop to 66,775 implies about 78,600 employees at the end of September 2025. A 12% drop from the second quarter implies about 75,900 at the end of June. Both are Jobs & Hire calculations from rounded percentages and should be treated as approximations, not reported counts.

Those implied figures suggest roughly 9,000 fewer employees between June and September, and nearly 12,000 fewer than a year earlier. The Next Web reported in May that Meta would cut about 8,000 jobs, around 10% of its workforce, beginning May 20, and cancel 6,000 open requisitions. The gap between the roughly 8,000 reported layoffs and the implied quarterly decline could reflect normal departures, rounding or other reductions. The sources reviewed do not break it down.

...

For employees, the practical point is that Meta has not committed to a stable headcount, and no executive has described a target size. For job seekers, it means current openings should be read as provisional.

...

A: 66,775 as of Sept. 30, 2026, down 15% from a year earlier, according to its earnings release.
